name: Facial Symmetry (Video)
description: Analyzes facial symmetry consistency in video
mechanism:
This method analyzes facial symmetry patterns in video for deepfake detection:

1. **Bilateral Feature Measurement**: Corresponding bilateral facial features are measured: left/right eye size, eyebrow position, cheek contour, nasolabial fold depth, lip corner position. The asymmetry (difference between left and right) is quantified for each feature pair.

2. **Natural Asymmetry Baseline**: All human faces exhibit natural bilateral asymmetry — typically 2-5% difference between sides. The method establishes per-subject asymmetry characteristics and checks whether they fall within normal ranges. Deepfakes may produce unnaturally symmetric faces (≈0% asymmetry) or exaggerated asymmetry inconsistent with natural variation.

3. **Pose-Adjusted Symmetry**: Apparent symmetry changes with head pose due to perspective projection. The method compensates for head pose to measure intrinsic facial symmetry. After correction, true facial asymmetry should remain constant regardless of viewing angle. Deepfakes may show pose-dependent symmetry changes indicating inconsistent 3D face modeling.

4. **Dynamic Symmetry Analysis**: During expressions, bilateral symmetry changes predictably — genuine smiles may be slightly asymmetric, surprise is relatively symmetric. The method analyzes dynamic symmetry patterns during expression events. Deepfakes may produce symmetric expressions when natural ones should be asymmetric, or vice versa.

5. **Temporal Symmetry Stability**: The subject's baseline facial asymmetry should remain constant across the video (bone structure doesn't change). The method tracks symmetry metrics temporally. Frame-to-frame variations in facial asymmetry — caused by independent generation of left and right face halves — indicate AI generation artifacts.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through facial symmetry (video) analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Matern, F. et al. (2019). Exploiting Visual Artifacts to Expose Deepfakes. WACVW.
Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
